title: A linked entry whose manufacturer no longer exists takes the one picked
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete' and See Financial Data.
  • Part Library entry {Part-A} (for example a number found in data saved before the release), with the description {Description-A} (for example the description shown on its row), still points to a manufacturer that no longer exists in this organization.
  • No other Part Library entry has exactly the number {Part-A}, with the same upper and lower case.
  • {Location-A} stocks no part whose number matches {Part-A} once upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces are ignored.
  • {Manufacturer-A} (for example the first name in the Manufacturer list) is a manufacturer offered in the Manufacturer list.
custom_steps:
1. At {Location-A}, go to Parts → Inventory and click New Inventory Part.
  2. Type {Description-A} in Description.
  3. Type {Part-A} in Part Number, exactly as written down.
  4. Open Manufacturer and pick {Manufacturer-A}.
  5. Pick any Category (for example Uncategorized).
  6. Type a Cost (for example 10.00).
  7. Click Save.
  8. Go to Parts → Part Library and type {Part-A} in the search.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 7: the part is saved and the window closes.
  • Step 8: still exactly one {Part-A} entry, and it now shows Manufacturer {Manufacturer-A}: an entry pointing to a manufacturer that no longer exists counts as having none.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S7-R6d, S7-R6b, Story 7 context note (S7-R6d), read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 1.3 (Number and description typed), board 7.1 (Part Library), 13 Oct copy. Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 11). Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S7-R6d: “A linked entry has a manufacturer only when it points to a manufacturer that exists in this organization. An entry that points to none takes the one picked in the dialog.”
  • S7-R6b: “A linked entry with no manufacturer takes the one picked in the dialog. An entry that already has a manufacturer keeps it.”
  • PRD Story 7 context note (S7-R6d): “Context note (S7-R6d): many existing entries point to a manufacturer that no longer exists. The data cleanup in SV-10033 runs before this feature is released. Manufacturers cannot be deleted in ShopView, so an entry pointing to a missing manufacturer comes only from data saved before the release.”
